question: One of the hereditary hypercoagulability states is due to the alteration of one of the following proteins, but NOT to the lack of it; which one?:
analysis: In hereditary hypercoagulability states, Factor V Leiden is due to the alteration of Factor V itself, leading to resistance to inactivation by protein C. This results in an increased risk of blood clot formation. The other options, Antithrombin, Protein C, and Protein S deficiencies, are due to the lack or reduced levels of these proteins, which can also predispose individuals to abnormal blood clotting.
